headline: An OpenAI engineer has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in an executive conference room, which officials say was meant to capture sensitive talks about the company's technology.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a criminal charge at a leading AI lab, confirmed by a court complaint, prosecutors, the FBI and OpenAI, with no sign yet that any model code or customer data was taken.
importance_line: OpenAI's staff and customers, and other AI labs, are affected because US officials call protecting AI technology from theft a national security priority, but the charge is an allegation, the complaint does not say what the recordings were for, and OpenAI says it has no sign that model weights, code or customer data were taken.
summary: The Associated Press reports that an OpenAI engineer, a 35-year-old Saudi national, was arrested on Friday 9 Oct 2026 and charged with using a device to intercept oral communications, after a recording device was found on 30 Sep 2026 hidden in a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco office. OpenAI says it used its own AI models to trace the device to the employee, fired him and told the FBI, and says it has no indication that he took model weights, source code or customer data; the complaint does not say what he meant to do with any recordings.
